# BMS / DJMax Keysound Slicer UX Audit

**Research boundary.** I treated a statement as a user pain point only when it was visible in a fetched README, issue, checklist, or hands-on guide. The Sayaslicer repository currently exposes six closed issues and no open results in the fetched issue views; therefore I do **not** invent a “top 10” issue list. PTSEQUENCER, FL Studio Slicer, iBMSC/BMSE internals, and YouTube comments were searched, but I found no sufficiently specific, fetchable primary evidence for several requested claims; those are marked **not verified** rather than inferred.

## 1. Comparison table

| Tool | Observed workflow | Top 3 pain points / limits evidenced | Max slices / snap | Export method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sayaslicer** | Load audio; place/move markers; optionally import BMHelper markers; preview; copy BMSE or iBMSC clipboard; export keysounds; save project. | (1) iBMSC’s arbitrary resolution can break after zero-crossing moves markers; README explicitly recommends BMSE clipboard when this causes missing keysounds or gamemode changes. (2) Very large files >2 GB had a bug report. (3) Linux preview and macOS launch had platform bugs. | Arbitrary snap from 1/1–1/192; no maximum slice count stated. Zero-crossing, fadeout, partial BPM changes, base-62 BMSE copy. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) | Hundreds of rendered keysound files plus BMSE/iBMSC clipboard data; project save/load. |
| **Woslicer II** | Drag WAV; set BPM; mark cuts on grid; preview; set starting definition number; export WAV batch; copy clipboard data; paste into BMSE. | (1) Manual marker placement. (2) Starting-number and file-order coordination is easy to get wrong. (3) Tail treatment is explicitly left for the user in the tutorial (“末端とかちゃんと調整”). | Guide documents default 16th grid and Woslicer III documents max 192 subdivisions; a Woslicer II slice-count cap was not stated. | Numbered WAV batch, then clipboard placement into BMSE. [Woslicer II guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) |
| **Woslicer III** | Choose BPM; drag WAV; click grid to add/remove cuts; press P to preview a segment; select resolution; export WAV; export `.wos`; copy clipboard; import files into BMSE; reuse definitions to reduce count. | (1) A cut’s tail can clip; the guide says fade processing is essential. (2) Definition reuse is a manual time cost. (3) Files/definitions must be kept in exact order and must not pass `#WAVZZ`; >1-minute keysounds are prohibited by the workflow. | Up to 192 subdivisions per bar; file numbering is normally 3 digits but 4+ can exist; no total slice cap stated. | WAV files, `.wos`, clipboard sequence; later WAV→OGG conversion. [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) |
| **BMHelper + Mid2BMS** | Export MIDI from DAW; import/analyze MIDI in BMHelper or use Mid2BMS; set minimum interval, sorting, similarity and multi-definition options; render WAV; copy cut positions to slicer; paste definitions and sequence into BMS editor; audition and repair. | (1) DAW export and multiple tool handoffs. (2) BMHelper’s clipboard-copy newline bug is documented; manual text-area copy is recommended. (3) BPM changes and automation make the workflow difficult; a Japanese workflow says BPM-change handling is “めちゃくちゃ苦労します” (extremely troublesome). | Mid2BMS workflow documents base-36 identifiers `01..ZZ` (1295); BMHelper uses user-set definition start and multi-definition spacing. Exact Mid2BMS slice cap not found. | Rendered WAVs plus generated BMS/clipboard definitions; users commonly convert WAV to OGG afterward. [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html), [workflow](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n03caf5d703f9) |
| **BMSE / iBMSC clipboard path** | Export clipboard text from slicer/helper; paste at the selected BMS position; save in editor. | (1) BMSE’s historical base-36 ceiling is `01..ZZ` = 1295 definitions. (2) iBMSC can preserve finer-than-192 positions but can expose compatibility problems when saved; BMSE rounds to nearest 192th. (3) Checklist warns default 192 partitioning can change sound if finer divisions were used. | 192 is the compatibility/rounding boundary in the cited checklist; BMSE base-62 support to 3843 is reported by NamuWiki, but player/editor compatibility is not guaranteed by that page. | Clipboard text, then external WAV/OGG files. [BMS checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/), [NamuWiki key sound](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) |
| **PTSEQUENCER** | Not verified from a fetchable primary source in this run. | The requested 2047-keysound limit was not independently verified; do not encode it as a product requirement without a source. | Not verified. | Not verified. |
| **sound-slicer** | Render a WAV from a text/MIDI description; run slicer; receive numbered WAVs and a BMS clipboard file; paste/transpose into editor. | (1) README explicitly says both supported styles do not support BPM changes. (2) It requires a folder convention and a `wav` subfolder. (3) It is batch/text-oriented rather than interactive waveform editing. | No snap maximum stated. | Numbered WAVs plus BMS clipboard file. [sound-slicer README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) |

## 2. Problem inventory

### Timeline

| Severity | Problem / evidence | Implication for DJMax Studio |
|---|---|---|
| **P0** | Traditional slicing has no single source of truth: the documented path renders WAVs, copies clipboard data, imports into BMSE, then checks playback. [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) | Keep `{sourceFile,startMs,endMs}` as the authoritative object; make file rendering a finalization step only. |
| **P0** | A 192nd save/rounding boundary can alter timing; the checklist explicitly warns that finer divisions sound different after snapping. [BMS checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/) | Preserve millisecond positions internally and show quantization loss before export. |
| **P1** | BPM changes are a known workflow hazard: one workflow says they are extremely difficult; sound-slicer says its styles do not support them. [workflow](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n03caf5d703f9), [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) | Use a tempo-map-aware bar/beat ruler plus an ms ruler; never assume one global BPM. |
| **P1** | Woslicer’s preview advances through markers, but the operator still manually creates cuts and later checks the result in BMSE/mBMPlay. [Woslicer II guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) | Synchronize waveform, slice preview, and chart preview with a single playhead. |
| **P1** | Zero-crossing reduces clicks but moves markers and can make iBMSC output fail. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) | Make zero-crossing a previewable per-slice override and expose the resulting time delta. |

### Interface / workflow

| Severity | Problem / evidence | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| **P0** | Users coordinate BPM, marker order, starting definition number, filesystem order, clipboard type, editor insertion point, and later definition cleanup. [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3), [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html) | One integrated “Slice Library” should own IDs, notes, source ranges, chart placements, and export names. |
| **P1** | Dragging files into BMSE depends on explorer sort order and selecting the correct first definition; the guide calls this out explicitly. [Woslicer workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) | Replace filename/order conventions with stable internal IDs and an import preview. |
| **P1** | Definition reuse reduces eight definitions to four in the guide, but requires a wizard and manual selection. [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) | Offer “reuse identical range/processed audio” with an explicit before/after count and undo. |
| **P1** | BMHelper documents a clipboard newline defect and advises copying from a text area instead. [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html) | Avoid text clipboard as the primary internal interchange; use a typed project format and keep clipboard only as compatibility export. |
| **P2** | Woslicer’s documented keyboard workflow is powerful but discoverability is low: `Z`, `P`, `Q/W`, arrows, `Enter`, `M`, `A/S` are separate controls. [Woslicer II guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) | Provide a visible shortcut overlay and configurable shortcuts; preserve fast keyboard operation. |

### Settings

| Severity | Problem / evidence | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | Existing tools expose snap/resolution, BPM, fade/tail behavior, zero-crossing, and definition spacing in different places and with different units. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer), [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html), [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) | Put Snap (1/4–1/192), Sensitivity, zero-cross, fade, normalize, and auto-advance in one toolbar/settings surface; allow per-slice overrides. |
| **P1** | Tail cutoff/clip is a real manual concern: the guide says abrupt tails clip and applies a fade to all keysounds. [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) | Default to non-destructive fade metadata; show waveform tail and audition before/after. |
| **P2** | The requested Sensitivity 0.55 and Normalize settings were not found in the fetched sources; do not claim competitor parity. | Treat these as proposed Studio settings requiring usability validation, not as evidence-backed existing-tool features. |

### Backend / format

| Severity | Problem / evidence | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| **P0** | BMS production requires each keysound under 60 seconds, and distribution commonly requires a folder full of separate audio files. [BMS checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/) | Enforce/flag duration at export, but let the draft remain a virtual slice over the intact source. |
| **P0** | Base-36 `01..ZZ` gives 1295 BMS definitions; NamuWiki reports BMSE’s 2024 pilot base-62 expansion to 3843. [NamuWiki key sound](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) | Use a format-neutral internal ID space; select BMS base-36/base-62 only in an export profile with capacity and compatibility warnings. |
| **P1** | OGG conversion is a separate post-processing step because WAV files are large. [BMS checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/) | Export WAV/OGG only on finalize, with deterministic naming and a manifest. |
| **P1** | Sayaslicer has platform-specific loading/preview bugs: >2GB load failure, Linux PortAudio preview failure, and macOS launch issue are visible in its closed issues. [closed issues](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed) | Stream/decode large audio, test preview backends separately, and provide actionable diagnostics. |
| **P1** | Key sounds can be interrupted when another sample arrives on a track in older rhythm-game implementations; NamuWiki explains the audible consequence and why effects/tails can be lost. [NamuWiki key sound](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) | Add overlap/interruption simulation for BMS, RESPECT, and TECHNIKA export modes. |

## 3. What Sayaslicer did right vs. Woslicer — keep these

**Keep from Sayaslicer:**
- Dual clipboard compatibility: BMSE for 192nd-safe output and iBMSC for finer arbitrary resolution. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)
- Arbitrary snapping plus a direct “resnap markers” operation. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer), [release notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/releases)
- Undo/redo, marker copy/cut/paste, project save/load, and keyboard-first navigation. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)
- Zero-crossing and fadeout as audio-quality aids, while warning that zero-crossing changes timing. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)
- Partial BPM-change support, even though the README calls it hackish and lists better support as planned. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)

**Keep from Woslicer/Woslicer III:**
- Immediate waveform interaction: drag/drop, grid cuts, segment preview, and batch output. [Woslicer II guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)
- A simple, visible workflow for definition numbering and clipboard placement. [Woslicer II guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)
- Reuse of definitions to control the BMS key limit. [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)
- `.wos` project export and a numbered WAV fallback that users can inspect. [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)

## 4. Top 10 recommendations for DJMax Studio Slicer

1. **Make virtual slices the source of truth (P0).** This directly removes the render/import ceremony evidenced by the Woslicer→BMSE workflow. [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)
2. **Implement the proposed dual timeline (P0):** waveform/ms ruler below, chart/bar-beat ruler above, shared playhead and zoom. BPM-change difficulty in existing workflows makes this the highest-leverage fix. [workflow](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n03caf5d703f9), [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)
3. **Add a Slice Library with stable IDs, source range, preview, chart placements, and reuse status (P0).** It replaces fragile explorer ordering and manual definition numbering. [Woslicer workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)
4. **Use a tempo-map-aware grid with Snap 1/4–1/192 plus raw-ms mode (P0).** Preserve precise positions internally and warn when an export rounds them. [BMS checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)
5. **Make zero-crossing non-destructive and per-slice (P1).** Preview the moved boundary, keep original start/end, and warn about timing/clipboard effects. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)
6. **Add per-slice Fade/Normalize/Zero-X overrides and a tail preview (P1).** Manual fade is explicitly required to prevent clipped tails. [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)
7. **Provide Auto-advance Grid / Beat / Off and retain keyboard-first editing (P1).** Woslicer’s preview-and-advance loop and Sayaslicer’s shortcuts show the value of rapid keyboard iteration. [Woslicer II guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)
8. **Add export profiles: BMS-36, BMS-62, RESPECT, TECHNIKA, and Studio-native (P1).** Capacity and interruption behavior differ across ecosystems; BMS-36 is 1295 while base-62 is reported as 3843 in BMSE pilot support. [NamuWiki key sound](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)
9. **Add an export validation report (P1):** >60-second slices, unsupported format, duplicate/reused definitions, quantization deltas, missing chart placements, and overlap/interruption risks. [BMS checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/), [NamuWiki key sound](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)
10. **Round-trip “Import to Studio” (P1).** Import generated chart placements and virtual slices back into the same project, rather than relying on clipboard text and external filenames; this addresses the documented handoff and copy/paste failure modes. [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)
